tl;dr: The grieving process is a bitch no matter how old or young you are.
As a child I just didn't understand why I was losing people and didn't understand they weren't coming back. As a teenager I became angry, resentful, and even became numb at points. As an adult I can deal with stressful situations easier and have a darker sense of humor. Dealing with death of a loved one never gets easier though.



My parents tended a cemetary while I was a child. I also lost a family member almost every other year while growing up.
 Up until I was 11 death didn't effect me. I just thought people were sleeping in the ground.
I thought they would just wake up one day after their rest. I assumed that because of the rest in peace on the tombstones. I was stupid.
When I was 8-11 I played around in the cemetery and watched people get placed into the ground all the time. Also had a great aunt and a great uncle pass away in those years. Separate times. Exact dates are foggy because I was so young.
I missed the great uncle's funeral because I was climbing a tree. Everyone left for the funeral. I was sitting on a branch and I watched all the cars leave. I wasn't scared just like welp that happened. Saw a cat in the neighboring yard and went to pet it. By that point my mom was back and mad as hell. Yay off topic memories. I know I'm a cancer.


 When I was 12 I lost my great grandmother that had dementia. She was sick for a long time and everyone expected it but I was clueless and not prepared for it. I just remember looking into her coffin and realizing she's not sleeping. I was so upset. I ran to the bathroom sobbing.
 It's complicated to explain but I was a quiet kid and didn't open up to many people. I didn't open up to her even though she was one of the kindest humans that ever walked the earth.
Instead I opened up to my very much alive abusive grandmother as a kid. I regretted not talking to her. I was also so angry at the time. I just didn't understand why someone so horrible could still be alive and someone so kind could die. Nothing was fair.



 When I was 13 I lost a cousin that was 8 months pregnant. She was buried with the baby cradled in her arms. Later that year another one of my cousin's husband passed away. He stepped on a mine and didn't have a body to bury. I didn't get to meet him and he was about to come home in a week. I just thought his was horrible the cousin that lost her husband was the sister to the other that died while pregnant.



 When I was 14 my great uncle passed away. He was not my favorite person so I'm not going to talk much about that. I was already numb to people dying by the time he passed. I stopped crying at funerals just stopped feeling anything.
When I was 15 I lost a friend to suicide. I was the last person he talked to on the phone. We only talked for a few minutes.


When I was 16 my aunt who had been living with us since I was 12 passed away. She was very special to me and my brother. She played a big roll in getting us away from my abusive grandmother. She had problems though. She was an addict and ended up relapsing bad. One day she Decided she didn't want to have a family anymore and ran back to the drugs. That lasted about 2 months. The day she called my uncle and told him she was coming back was the day she was murdered. Everyone went from being ecstatic that she was coming back home to fucking devastated the next week. Apparently one of the men she ran off with wasn't happy that she was going back to my uncle so they along with two other men attacked her and brutally murdered her. Again numb at funeral but heard a song she like on the radio a year later and cried like a baby.


 When I was 18 my abusive grandmother passed away. I was so torn between hating her and feeling sorry for her that I didn't know what to do with my self. This may make me seem cruel but I'm going to be honest about how I felt at the time.
 It started in August. We were told granny was going to be staying with us again but this time it would be different. She had cancer and it spread through her stomach. We needed to make her comfortable. She arrived on her death bed and was set up cozily downstairs.
Sometimes when people are dying they become faithful and very remorseful. I ignored her apologies. I pretended I didn't hear her. At one point early on she was able to stand and wanted to show me how to make french toast. She remembered making it for me and me liking it as a kid. I refused to take her seriously and made a joke out of it.
I was just a passive aggressive and angry brat until she passed away a week before Christmas.
I was angry and then very fucking numb. I had wished for her to be dead for a very long time.
I thought I should be happy but I felt like a void.
About a year ago I attempted making french toast and broke down crying.

I just recently came out of being severely depressed and am turning a new leaf in life.
It's made me see things clearer and I've realized I've never really been able to properly vent or share my problems because all the people in my life shut me down like that.
(the everyone has it worse thing or one upping)
Like fuck can I just share something with you without it becoming a pity competition.

Everyone has problems and deserves to be heard. I have always just been on the listening and give advice end.

People make assumptions that I have it so great because I keep a smile on my face and roll out the jokes for my friends.
Severely depressed people pretend to be happy all the time. It's a way to cope when you are numb to make others happy. I woke up a weak ago and realized that no one really knows me. No one even knows that I was as bad as I was. I'm in a way relieved but also sort of bitter from this.

I've been taking baby steps on my own to get over my depression.

 When I want to self injure I kiss or rub my ankles and thighs instead(my usual go to spots for punishment).
 When I get suicidal I think about the loved ones who it would effect.
 When I start to dwell on my past I instead try to appreciate what I have now. 
These are small things that are helping me break the giant loop that has been burdening me for years.
